C_product_page_copy.hero_summary: NAD+ is nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, a dinucleotide coenzyme that sits at the center of cellular redox chemistry. It is not a peptide, and a lot of vendor pages get that wrong. Veracue supplies NAD+ as a laboratory research material under CAS 53-84-9, for in vitro and preclinical work only. It is not for human or veterinary use, not for diagnostic use, and not for any therapeutic application.

sections.heading: What NAD+ is, and what it is not
body: NAD+ is built from two nucleotides, one carrying nicotinamide and one carrying adenine, joined through a ribose-phosphate-phosphate-ribose bridge. That structure puts it in the dinucleotide class. Peptides are chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. NAD+ contains neither.

The distinction matters for more than terminology. It changes which analytical methods mean anything. Sequence confirmation, truncation analysis and amino acid analysis are peptide tools. For NAD+ the relevant questions are anomeric configuration, redox state, water content and chromatographic purity under a stated method.
Four related molecules get confused with NAD+ constantly, often in ways that move evidence from one compound to another where it does not belong.

Read that table once and a common error becomes visible. Most published human trial data described as NAD+ research was generated with NR or NMN, not with NAD+. Precursor results are not NAD+ results.

rows: The reduced form of the same coenzyme
Redox partner. Same molecule, different electron state
A separate cofactor system, mostly anabolic. Not interchangeable
Distinct from NADH in its metabolic role
Released when NAD+ is consumed, and fed back through salvage
An upstream precursor, converted toward NMN
The immediate precursor, converted to NAD+ by NMNAT

sections.heading: Why two molecular weights show up for the same compound
body: This trips people up during molar calculations, so it is worth spelling out.

The plus sign in NAD+ refers to the positive charge on the nicotinamide ring nitrogen. Written strictly as that cation, the formula is C21H28N7O14P2+ with an average mass of 664.44. Most chemical databases, including PubChem CID 5892, publish the neutral inner-salt form instead, where a phosphate oxygen carries the balancing negative charge. That representation is C21H27N7O14P2 at 663.43.
Same substance. Same CAS. One proton apart in bookkeeping.

There is a second, larger correction that matters more in practice. Published molecular weights are anhydrous values. beta-NAD is commonly supplied as a hydrate, and water content can be a meaningful fraction of what is in the vial. If a protocol needs an accurate molar concentration, the calculation needs the supplier's water content figure, not just the catalog MW. Salt forms shift the number again.
Researchers should work from the specification sheet for the lot in hand rather than a database value.

sections.heading: What NAD+ does in cells
body: Two roles, and they are worth separating because they lead to different research questions.

As a redox cofactor. NAD+ accepts a hydride to become NADH, and NADH donates electrons downstream. That NAD+/NADH couple runs through glycolysis, the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. It is the reason NAD+ appears in almost every bioenergetics protocol ever written.

As a consumed co-substrate. Three enzyme families cleave NAD+ rather than cycling it. Sirtuins (SIRT1 through SIRT7) use it for deacetylation and related deacylation reactions. PARPs use it during DNA damage sensing and repair, and can draw down large NAD+ pools when strongly activated. CD38 and CD157 act as NADases, producing ADP-ribose and cyclic ADP-ribose. Each of these reactions releases nicotinamide, which feeds back into the salvage pathway.

Cells rebuild NAD+ through three routes. The de novo route starts from tryptophan through the kynurenine pathway. The Preiss-Handler route starts from nicotinic acid. The salvage pathway dominates in mammals, converting nicotinamide to NMN through NAMPT, then NMN to NAD+ through NMNAT.

None of this is a claim about what happens when NAD+ is administered to an organism. Biochemical centrality is not a therapeutic outcome, and compartmentalization means an increase in one pool does not imply an increase in another.

sections.heading: Research applications
body: NAD+ appears as a reagent, a substrate or a measured analyte across several fields.
These are research contexts. None of them is a statement that purchasing this material produces a physiological result.
list: Enzyme kinetics. As the cofactor in dehydrogenase assays, where NADH formation is tracked spectrophotometrically
Redox biology. NAD+/NADH ratio measurement in cells, tissues and isolated mitochondria
Sirtuin research. As the obligate co-substrate in deacetylation assays
PARP and DNA damage biology. Following NAD+ consumption during PARP activation
CD38 and NADase work. Substrate for cyclase and hydrolase activity assays
Metabolomics. As an analytical standard for NAD-pathway metabolite panels
Comparative pathway studies. Alongside NMN, NR and nicotinamide, where the distinction between compounds is the point of the experiment

sections.heading: Analytical verification, and what each test actually proves
body: This is where most vendor pages stop at a percentage. A percentage on its own does not tell a researcher much, because different methods measure different things and each one leaves a specific blind spot.

rows: RP-HPLC with UV detection, reported as area %
Chromatographic purity under one stated column, mobile phase and detection wavelength
Molecular identity. Anything that does not elute or does not absorb. Water content. Salt form
A measured mass consistent with the expected molecule
Accurate mass plus fragmentation consistent with the expected structure
Absolute purity. Anomeric configuration, since alpha-NAD and beta-NAD share a mass
Redox state. NADH absorbs strongly near 340 nm, NAD+ effectively does not
Purity against impurities that do not absorb in that region
Enzymatic assay tracking change in A340
Functional NAD+ content, using the NADH extinction coefficient of roughly 6.2 to 6.3 x 10^3 L per mol per cm
The identity of whatever is not NAD+
Water content, which converts an as-supplied figure to an anhydrous-basis figure

consequences.point: Chromatographic purity and content are different numbers.
consequences.explanation: An HPLC area percentage says what fraction of the detected peak area belongs to the main peak. An assay value says how much NAD+ is actually present per unit mass. A hydrated material can show excellent chromatographic purity and still deliver less anhydrous NAD+ per milligram than the label implies.

consequences.point: Mass alone cannot resolve the anomer.
consequences.explanation: beta-NAD is the biologically active configuration. The alpha-anomer is an isomer with an identical molecular mass, so mass spectrometry will not separate them. Chromatographic resolution or an enzymatic assay is what settles that question.

consequences.point: Redox state needs its own check.
consequences.explanation: NAD+ and NADH differ by two mass units and behave very differently in the UV. A supplier claiming NAD+ should be able to show that the material is in the oxidized state.

sections.heading: Stability and handling
body: NAD+ is hygroscopic, and the degradation routes are well characterized in the literature. The factors that matter are below.

Those are general properties of the compound. Storage instructions for a specific product should come from that product's own specification sheet, which accounts for its form, water content and packaging.
list: Moisture. Absorbed water accelerates hydrolysis. This is the main reason supplier documentation emphasizes sealed, desiccated storage
Temperature. Degradation speeds up with heat. Supplier specifications commonly call for cold storage of the solid, with lower temperatures for longer holds
pH. Stability is best near neutral to slightly acidic. Base-catalyzed cleavage of the N-glycosidic bond accelerates above neutral
Light. UV and near-UV exposure can drive photodegradation, which is why amber or foil protection is standard
Solution state. Reconstituted NAD+ is less stable than the solid. Keep solutions cold, protected from light, and avoid alkaline buffers and repeated freeze-thaw

sections.heading: Human evidence, stated accurately
body: Direct NAD+ administration and NAD precursor administration are separate evidence bases. Conflating them is the most common error in NAD content, and it usually runs in one direction, taking the larger precursor literature and presenting it as support for NAD+ itself.

evidence_table.study: Single-center randomized placebo-controlled trial, 180 adults with ischemic cardiomyopathy, LVEF 45% or below, NYHA II to III
evidence_table.result: Greater improvement in LVEF at 1 month versus placebo, 45.44 +/- 8.55% vs 42.44 +/- 9.09%, p = 0.024
evidence_table.limitation: Single center. Surrogate imaging endpoint. Every secondary endpoint was a non-significant trend: NT-proBNP p = 0.102, composite events 14.6% vs 24.7% p = 0.089, first HF hospitalization 13.5% vs 23.6% p = 0.078, NYHA class at 6 months p = 0.097

evidence_table.study: Open-label pilot, 11 male participants (8 infused, 3 control)
evidence_table.result: No change in plasma NAD+ or its metabolites until after 2 hours. Increased urinary excretion of methylnicotinamide and NAD+ at 6 hours
evidence_table.limitation: Pharmacokinetic only. Very small. No clinical outcomes. The authors described the plasma result as surprising

evidence_table.study: Randomized study, 60 older heart failure patients, Rev Cardiovasc Med 2024
evidence_table.result: Reported improvement rates in NT-proBNP and LVEF

evidence_table.study: Review of human ageing evidence, Nature Metabolism, October 2025
evidence_table.result: Precursors reliably raise NAD-related metabolites. Human clinical trials have shown limited efficacy
evidence_table.limitation: This is precursor evidence. It does not transfer to NAD+

sections.what_the_evidence_does_not_show: There is no established human outcome evidence for NAD+ in ageing, energy, cognition, body composition or athletic performance. The same Nature Metabolism review notes that even the premise of an age-related NAD+ decline in humans has been consistently observed in only a limited number of studies, and that human tissue-level data remains sparse. Mechanism is not outcome. Preclinical is not clinical. Precursor is not NAD+.

sections.heading: Regulatory position
body: NAD+ is not approved by the FDA as a drug for any indication.

In September 2019 the FDA proposed that nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, along with reduced NADH disodium, not be included on the 503A bulk drug substances list (Federal Register, docket FDA-2018-N-4845). That proposal has not been finalized, and NAD remains on the Category 1 list of substances under evaluation, which is why compounded NAD+ preparations continue to exist under the FDA's interim enforcement policy. NAD does not appear on the final 503A list at 21 CFR 216.23.

Two separations worth holding onto. Regulatory status attaching to compounded injectable NAD+ preparations is not the same as the status of a laboratory research material. And the regulatory histories of NMN and NR are separate again, and cannot be read across to NAD+.
Veracue is not a compounding pharmacy and does not operate as a compounding facility under Section 503A.

sections.heading: Research use boundary
body: NAD+ supplied by Veracue is for in vitro laboratory and preclinical research only. It is not a drug, a dietary supplement, a cosmetic or a food product. It is not approved by the FDA or any regulatory body for human or veterinary use, diagnosis, treatment, cure or prevention of any disease or condition. It must not be administered to humans or animals.

Nothing on this page is medical advice, and no statement here should be read as a therapeutic or health claim. By purchasing, the buyer confirms they are a qualified researcher, laboratory or institution acquiring this material for lawful research purposes, and accepts responsibility for compliance with applicable local, state and federal regulations.

D_faq.question: What is NAD+?
D_faq.answer: NAD+ is nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide in its oxidized form, a coenzyme found in every living cell. It works as a redox cofactor in energy metabolism and as a consumed co-substrate for sirtuins, PARPs and CD38. Veracue supplies it as a laboratory research material under CAS 53-84-9.

D_faq.question: Is NAD+ a peptide?
D_faq.answer: No. NAD+ is a dinucleotide coenzyme, built from a nicotinamide nucleotide and an adenine nucleotide joined through a ribose-phosphate bridge. It contains no amino acids and no peptide bonds. Several vendor sites label it a peptide. That label is incorrect.

D_faq.question: What is the difference between NAD+ and NADH?
D_faq.answer: They are the two redox states of the same coenzyme. NAD+ is the oxidized form and accepts a hydride to become NADH, the reduced form. NADH then donates electrons downstream. The pair is usually written as the NAD+/NADH couple. They are easy to tell apart in the UV, because NADH absorbs strongly near 340 nm and NAD+ effectively does not.

D_faq.question: Is NAD+ the same as NMN?
D_faq.answer: No. NMN, nicotinamide mononucleotide, is the immediate precursor to NAD+ in the salvage pathway, converted by the enzyme NMNAT. NMN has the formula C11H15N2O8P at 334.22 g/mol, roughly half the mass of NAD+. Research results generated with NMN are not results for NAD+.

D_faq.question: Is NAD+ the same as NR?
D_faq.answer: No. NR, nicotinamide riboside, is an upstream precursor that is converted toward NMN and then to NAD+. NR has the formula C11H15N2O5+ at 255.25 g/mol for the free base, and is usually sold as the chloride salt at 290.70. Like NMN, it is a different compound with its own evidence base.

D_faq.question: What is the difference between NAD+ and NADP+?
D_faq.answer: NADP+ is a separate phosphorylated cofactor with the formula C21H28N7O17P3+ at roughly 744.4 g/mol. It carries an extra phosphate group and serves largely anabolic and antioxidant pathways, while NAD+ serves catabolic energy metabolism. The two are not interchangeable, and neither are their reduced forms NADPH and NADH.

D_faq.question: What is the molecular weight and CAS number of NAD+?
D_faq.answer: The CAS number is 53-84-9. Molecular weight depends on how the molecule is written. As the cation C21H28N7O14P2+ it is 664.44 g/mol. As the neutral inner-salt form C21H27N7O14P2, which is what PubChem CID 5892 publishes, it is 663.43 g/mol. Both figures are anhydrous values, so hydrated material needs a water-content correction for accurate molar work.

D_faq.question: Why does the molecular weight on my calculation not match the label?
D_faq.answer: Usually one of three reasons. The catalog figure is anhydrous and the material is hydrated. The material is a salt form with a different mass. Or the two published representations, cation and zwitterion, are being mixed. Check the supplier specification for form and water content before calculating molarity.

D_faq.question: How is NAD+ tested for identity and purity?
D_faq.answer: Typically by reverse-phase HPLC with UV detection for chromatographic purity, and by mass spectrometry for identity. A UV scan can confirm redox state, and an enzymatic assay tracking absorbance change at 340 nm can measure functional NAD+ content. Karl Fischer titration measures water content where the material is hydrated.

D_faq.question: Does HPLC alone prove the identity of a NAD+ sample?
D_faq.answer: No. HPLC reports what fraction of the detected peak area corresponds to the main peak under one specific method. It does not identify the molecule, and it does not see anything that fails to elute or fails to absorb at the detection wavelength. Mass spectrometry adds a measured mass consistent with the expected structure. Even combined, the two cannot separate the alpha and beta anomers, which share a molecular mass. That takes chromatographic resolution or an enzymatic assay.

D_faq.question: What should a NAD+ certificate of analysis contain?
D_faq.answer: Product name and CAS, the specific form, a lot number matching the vial, the test date and issuing laboratory, a purity result with the method named, an assay or content result, water content where relevant, identity confirmation, and specification limits to read the results against. A purity figure with no method attached is not verification.

D_faq.question: What should researchers verify before purchasing NAD+ research material?
D_faq.answer: Four things. That the supplier states the form, since free acid, salt and hydrate carry different masses. That purity and content are reported as separate numbers with methods named. That identity is confirmed by an orthogonal method, not chromatography alone. And that a lot-specific document exists for the vial being shipped, not a generic sample document.
